summary: Maho Iuchi specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Otani University (~2003–2008) and held a visiting researcher post at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, attested in 2010.
Mai Mishiro is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. She held affiliations with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested in 2011) and Waseda University (attested in 2016).

Makio Takemura is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned master's and doctoral degrees at the University of Tokyo and studied under Ryōmin Akizuki. He served as professor at the University of Tsukuba and president of Toyo University (2009–2020).

Makio Ueno specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having completed his PhD at Otani University by 2009. He held posts at the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute, Otani University, and Otani Academic Society.

Makoto Funaoka studied at Meiji University (~1965–1977), working across philosophy, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He held teaching posts at The Open University of Japan, Komazawa University, and served as professor emeritus at Hokkai-Gakuen University (1993–2017).

Makoto Kitada is an Indologist and linguist who completed doctoral studies at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. Kitada has been affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2008–2010) and Osaka University (attested 2026).

Makoto Nagai was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1934–1942), Nihon University, Toyo University, Kamakura Women's University, and president of Chuo Shoka Junior College.
Makoto Yoshimura, a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology, completed his doctoral course at Waseda University (~1993–1998). Around 2004, he served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University.
Malati J. Shendge was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale, R. D. Vadekar, and received guidance from Akira Hirakawa.

Malcolm David Eckel is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Oxford and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and served on the faculty at Boston University from 1990 to 2024.

Mallica Kumbera Landrus specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. As of 2026, she is attested as Keeper of Eastern Art and Associate Professor of Indian Art at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford.
Mamata Dash is a scholar in the field of Indology who completed her studies at Ravenshaw Girls' School and Utkal University.

Mamoru Tonami was a scholar of sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University under Ichisada Miyazaki. He held assistant, associate, and full professor posts at Kyoto University (1965–2001) and taught at Otani University.
Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist who served as General Secretary of The Asiatic Society. He also worked at Jadavpur University as the Co-ordinator of DSA Sanskrit, attested in 2003.

Manabu Asano is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a PhD student at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2020) and serves as a researcher at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Manasi Dilip Nadkarni is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. Attested in 2026, she studied under doctoral supervisor Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and held a post as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

Mandan Mishra was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as principal at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University (~1967–1989), Vice-Chancellor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1993–1997), and held a post at the University of Rajasthan.

Manfred Mayrhofer was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Wilhelm Brandenstein at the University of Graz. He served as an ordentlicher Professor at Saarland University (1962–1966) and the University of Vienna (1966–1990).

Manfred Taube was a Tibetologist and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at the University of Leipzig under Friedrich Weller. In 1991, he became Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Philology at Leipzig.

Mangal Deva Shastri was an Indologist and linguist who earned a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (1919–1922) under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from approximately 1931 to 1946.
